knowledge:
- key_parameters: exprs_file=Path to the input expression file (supports TPM and CPM formats in a tab- or space-delimited text file) ;; log_transform=Logical, whether to log2-transform the input expression data (default TRUE) ;; remove_outliers=Logical, whether to remove outlier cells during pre-processing (default TRUE) ;; preliminary_sorting_method=Method for preliminary cell ordering, options: "autoSPIN", "sWanderlust", "monocle", "Wanderlust", "SPIN", "none" ;; refine_sorting_method=Method for refined cell ordering, options: "autoSPIN", "sWanderlust", "monocle", "Wanderlust", "SPIN", "none" ;; project_name=Character string for the project name, used in output file naming (default "uSORT") ;; result_directory=Directory path where results and plots will be saved (default getwd()) ;; save_results=Logical, whether to save result files and plots to disk (default TRUE) ;; reproduce_seed=Integer seed for reproducibility (default 1234)
- alternatives: The package incorporates several alternative sorting methods internally that users can choose from, including autoSPIN, sWanderlust, monocle, Wanderlust, and SPIN.
- when_to_use: Appropriate for single-cell RNA-seq transcriptomics datasets (specifically TPM or CPM values) where the user wants to order cells along an intrinsic progression path (pseudotime/trajectory) and identify driver/signature genes.
- pitfalls: Input file format must be a text file containing TPM or CPM values. On macOS, launching the GUI requires tcltk support. Ensure save_results = TRUE if you want to automatically generate and save the PDF plots (e.g., distance heatmaps and driver gene profiles).

workflows.name: usort_cell_progression
workflows.intent: Uncover the intrinsic cell progression path and identify driver genes from single-cell RNA-seq expression data.
input: exprs_file.txt (text file containing TPM or CPM single-cell RNA-seq expression matrix)
signature_genes.txt (optional text file containing known signature genes for validation)
celltype.txt (optional text file containing cell type annotations for validation)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the package and locate the input expression file ;; 2. Run the main uSORT function to perform pre-processing, preliminary gene selection, preliminary cell ordering, refined gene selection, and refined cell ordering ;; 3. Extract and inspect the resulting list containing raw expression, trimmed log2 expression, preliminary/refined sorting genes, and preliminary/refined cell orders ;; 4. (Optional) Validate and visualize the preliminary and refined cell orderings using known signature genes and cell type annotations via heatmaps
